standard.title: Rehearse and perform with genre skills
standard.description: rehearse and perform dance for audiences, using technical and expressive skills and genre- or style-specific techniques
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can rehearse and perform dance for audiences using technical and expressive skills and genre/style-specific techniques (Y7-8, AC9ADA8P01). They have worked with production elements, rehearsal strategies and performed in formal and informal contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students rehearse and perform dance for audiences, using technical and expressive skills and genre- or style-specific techniques.

nodes.label: Performance entry/exit and spatial fluency
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan and execute performance entry and exit in ways consistent with genre/style, mood or the ideas conveyed in the dance.
nodes.minimum_width: Planning and executing a performance entry and exit that is consistent with the genre/style and communicative intent of the dance.
nodes.typical_width: Planning how to enter and leave the performance space consistently with genre/style, mood or ideas conveyed; building confidence in accurate and fluent spatial placement maintenance throughout performance; using rehearsal to develop fluency and consistency.
wider: Choreograph the entry and exit as deliberate compositional elements — using them to establish and resolve the performance's communicative arc
Rehearse spatial placement and entry/exit in a range of performance space configurations — developing adaptable performance spatial awareness

response_modes.reason: Spatial fluency in performance requires repetition in realistic performance conditions — not just rehearsal room practice. Simulate performance conditions (including entry/exit) in rehearsals.

success_criteria: Student enters and exits the performance space in a way that is consistent with the genre/style and communicative intent
Student maintains accurate spatial placement throughout performance

nodes.label: Genre/style technique in performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply genre- or style-specific techniques with technical and expressive skill in formal performance — communicating ideas, perspectives or meaning authentically within the style.
nodes.minimum_width: Performing in a selected genre/style with at least two identifiable style-specific techniques — demonstrating both technical quality and expressive communication.
nodes.typical_width: Applying technical and expressive skills and genre- or style-specific techniques when performing learned and/or choreographed dances; using available production elements (music, costume, props) to enhance communication of ideas, perspectives or meaning.
wider: Perform in a culturally specific genre/style with input or guidance from community representatives — demonstrating authentic engagement beyond surface imitation
Perform in more than one genre/style context during the year — comparing the performance demands and audience relationships each context creates
nodes.hinge_reason: Genre/style-authentic performance — not just technically competent movement — is the standard for this band. Students who cannot yet apply style-specific technique in performance context have not met the descriptor's demand and are not prepared for post-school performance or arts industry pathways.

response_modes.reason: Genre-authentic performance integrates technical skill, expressive skill, style-specific technique, and production element use into a communicative event. The audience relationship is the test: does this read as this style/genre to an informed observer?

success_criteria: Student applies at least two genre- or style-specific techniques recognisably in performance
Student uses at least one production element purposefully — enhancing rather than distracting from the communicative intent
Student's performance communicates the intended ideas, perspectives or meaning — evidenced through audience response or reflection
